testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: To leave a parking space as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can pull forward to leave.
On the side of a road, not in a parking lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous. Park so you can pull forward to exit your space whenever possible.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything about crossings.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Even if your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even with ABS on just one axle, you have more braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require you to inspect your vehicle before every trip, no matter how long.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before your trip, check each slack adjuster by pulling it. It should not move more than about one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs to be fixed.

questions.question: Front tires must have a tread depth of at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need 4/32 of an inch tread depth on front tires and 2/32 of an inch on other tires for safe operation.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Will prevent turn signals from working.

questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps axles in place. Damaged parts like leaking shock absorbers are potentially dangerous defects.

questions.question: A fatigued driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake.
May make important decisions too slowly.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes you slower to see hazards and react to them. You will have trouble making quick, important decisions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tire problem to check for?

options.text: Using radial and bias-ply tires together
Recapped tires on the front of a school bus
All tires made by the same company

questions.correctAnswerText: All tires made by the same company
questions.explanation: Check for low or high air pressure, excessive wear, cuts, tread separation, dual tires touching each other, mismatched tire sizes, radial and bias-ply tires together, damaged valve stems, and recapped tires on school bus front wheels.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used after crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used near tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers before approaching and crossing railroad tracks. Turn them off after your entire vehicle clears the tracks.

questions.question: Routine vehicle inspections should be done to ensure:
questions.explanation: Vehicle inspections are important to keep you and other drivers safe on the road.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. Texting distracts your mind and also takes your eyes off the road.

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Veer from your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Reduce your speed after entering the curve.
Refrain from looking for other vehicles while turning.
Reduce your speed before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Do not brake or shift gears while in the curve. Stay in your lane and check for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, a driver should look under the vehicle:

options.text: To see if the vehicle is on an incline.
To see if there are any fresh fluids on the ground.
To see if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if there are any fresh fluids on the ground.
questions.explanation: Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check for anything that could be hazardous, such as people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires.

questions.question: When using road speed to know when to switch gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds each gear is good for and shift up when necessary.
Watch other vehicles and try to keep pace.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as a guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds each gear is good for and shift up when necessary.
questions.explanation: Learn which speeds work best for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift to a higher gear as you go faster.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Drivers are least alert late at night, especially after midnight. Tired driving crashes happen more often at night than any other time.

questions.question: Over-the-counter medication:

options.text: Poses no safety risks to a driver.
Is not referenced by any laws regarding driving under the influence.
Can affect a person's ability to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect a person's ability to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can have side effects that make it unsafe to drive. It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance, including some over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation:

options.text: The State will inform your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a driver should:

options.text: Watch for people getting out of vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people getting out of vehicles.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. A person may open a door or step out from between vehicles without checking for traffic. A driver may start moving their vehicle before noticing you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To protect the cargo from weather
To keep the cargo a secret

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep the cargo a secret
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather. Keeping cargo secret is not a valid reason to cover it.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and signals, follow all laws, and avoid accidents and moving violations.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus. They are only allowed on the rear.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash.
Protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: The ____ shows how much air pressure is in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. It shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on road surfaces is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road shows through it, so it looks wet. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Once air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Begin pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air once tanks reach about 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Check local laws to make sure emergency flashers are allowed.

questions.question: When loading cargo, weight should be placed:
questions.explanation: A vehicle can tip over if its center of gravity is too high. Spread cargo weight evenly and keep it as low as possible to prevent tipping.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction is created when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: The two indicators that tell you when to upshift are:

options.text: Oil pressure and air brake pressure.

questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your manual to learn when to shift at the top of the rpm range. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds each gear handles, then watch your speedometer and shift as needed.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, you should:

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Not use gloves to touch the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant to a system without a recovery tank. Wear gloves or use a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: Which of these determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully when near road workers.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify an applicant from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Several crimes will disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations. Serious crimes like murder result in lifetime disqualification.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, you can help by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When visibility is low, turn your headlights on to low beam. If you cannot see others well, they likely cannot see you well either.

questions.question: Rolling backward when you start to accelerate is dangerous because:

options.text: The truck is not made to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can accelerate without rolling back. Rolling backwards can cause you to hit a vehicle or obstacle behind your truck.

questions.question: When driving long distances, you should:
questions.explanation: Take a break after every 100 miles or two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving through the night or when you would normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: Which of these is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire with one or two missing lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and needs to be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and needs to be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also unsafe. Check that your tires and rims are in good condition before driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks during a driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: Always turn on your emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This warns other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: Bridges usually:
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces. Be extra careful on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Each system has separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks but have separate hoses and lines.
Each system uses the same lines and hoses.
One system is main, and a second system backs it up if the first fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move or warn you with their horns if you did not see them. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Non-front tires on a commercial motor vehicle must have a tread depth of at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must have a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch on front tires and 2/32 of an inch on all other tires for safe operation.

questions.question: Containerized loads are used:

options.text: When cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
When cargo has been or will be transported by train.

questions.correctAnswerText: When cargo has been or will be transported by train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are usually used when freight is carried partly by rail or ship. You cannot inspect sealed containers, but you must make sure the containers do not exceed safe and legal weight limits.

questions.question: Spring brakes come on:

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When a dashboard control is activated.
When tires have minimal tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. Do not wait for this to happen. As soon as you see a low pressure warning, safely exit the road and stop your vehicle while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs placed on a vehicle to identify cargo hazards.
A type of tire used in snowy conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs placed on a vehicle to identify cargo hazards.
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the specific hazard class of the cargo.
